syntax: poisson()/nbinom2() with phylo(1 | group, tree = tree)
claim_boundary: Large-p phylogenetic random-intercept counts. Measured against native TMB at p = 20, 300, 1000 and 3000, all PARITY_PASS (coef 6.4e-08 to 1.0e-05; logLik ~1e-09). NARROW, and the boundary must stay visible: (a) RESOLVED 2026-08-25 -- a Julia-side standing gate now exists (test/test_phylo_count_largep_gate.jl, wired, 23 pass + 1 broken, 7.5s); it is a recovery/regression gate, NOT parity (parity stays with the R harness), and it round-trips re_sd across tree heights 0.8/1.6/4.0 to catch the raw-vs-normalised covariance trap -- verified to fire on the injected mistake (spread 2.236x = sqrt(4.0/0.8)) and not on correct behaviour (1.08x); (b) SE parity appears to LOOSEN from ~8e-06 relative at p=300 to ~1.5e-03 at p>=1000 while coef and logLik do not (DRM.jl#487, soft measurement -- the probe emitted display-rounded SEs); (c) p=3000 is two orders of magnitude below DRM.jl's own p=10,000 O(p) claim and NO native comparator has been attempted near that scale. NOTE the dense-O(p^3) premise is measurably false here: native TMB scaled O(p^1.27) over this range (DRM.jl#486), so this is genuine parity, not a DRM.jl-only reach. NOT interval coverage. NEW AND MORE SERIOUS, found by writing that gate (DRM.jl#491): fit.converged is TRUE at p=128 and FALSE for every p >= 192, while the estimates get BETTER. _laplace_outer_converged compares a flat limit (1e-4*(1+norm(theta,Inf)) ~ 1.6e-4) against a gradient that grows linearly with n (9.07e-5 / 1.91e-4 / 3.68e-4 at n = 512/1024/2048) while the RELATIVE gradient is flat (1.21e-7 / 1.33e-7 / 1.39e-7). The g_tol*n term written to handle this is ~30x too small to win the max() and first binds near n=16,000. THIS IS WHY THE ROW STAYS `partial`: it is a claim about LARGE p, and at large p the route tells the user it did not converge. VERIFIED 2026-08-25: the R harness records 14 columns and NONE is convergence, so every PARITY_PASS in parity-classc.tsv was recorded without consulting the flag. But that cuts the reassuring way, and the earlier wording here had it backwards: TMB and DRM.jl agreeing to 6.4e-08 on coefficients means both optimisers landed on the SAME point, which is positive evidence the fits are AT the optimum. Two different optimisers stopping at the same wrong place is not a credible coincidence. So the parity numbers are sound, and they CORROBORATE #491 as a reporting bug rather than a fitting failure -- the fit is right and the flag is wrong. The gap in the harness is that it cannot tell you the flag was false, not that its numbers are suspect. SHARPER, measured 2026-08-25: the flag is ANTI-CORRELATED with care in this regime. On identical data at p=512, g_tol=1e-8 (the default) gives converged=FALSE at relative gradient 1.39e-07, while g_tol=10.0 gives converged=TRUE at 1.18e-03 -- four orders of magnitude worse. Cause: _laplace_outer_converged short-circuits on `Optim.converged(res) && return true`, and a loose g_tol makes Optim's own criterion trivially satisfiable. So the flag answers 'did the optimiser meet the tolerance you asked for', and asking for LESS makes it easier to say yes. A relative criterion does separate cleanly (1.2e-07..1.5e-07 for careful fits vs 1.18e-03 at g_tol=10), so any threshold in 1e-06..1e-05 works with orders of magnitude of margin. Mitigating: the ESTIMATES barely move (b1 = 0.2894 identical to 4 dp at g_tol = 1e-8, 1e-1 and 1.0), so this is a REPORTING defect, not a fitting one. Not fixed here -- the threshold and the short-circuit's removal both move the accept/reject boundary for every family on the sparse-Laplace path, which is an owner's call, but it can now be made against numbers.
